skill.name: to-prd
skill.description: Turn an existing product or engineering conversation into a structured PRD and publish it to the project issue tracker.
skill.summary: Create a PRD from existing discussion, codebase context, testing decisions, and issue tracker requirements.
skill.author: mattpocock

finding_verdicts.reason: The flagged text is Markdown inline code for a slash command name, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. No executable script or command interpolation appears in SKILL.md line 9.
The flagged text is Markdown inline code around a label name, not shell execution. It describes applying an issue tracker label and contains no executable code path.

content.value_statement: Teams lose product detail when decisions stay scattered across chat and code review. This skill turns existing context into a structured PRD for the issue tracker.
actual_capabilities: Synthesizes the current conversation into a PRD without running a new interview.
Uses repository context and domain vocabulary when the agent has already inspected the codebase.
Prompts for confirmation on proposed testing seams before final publication.
Formats the PRD with problem, solution, user stories, implementation decisions, testing decisions, scope, and notes.
Guides publication to the configured project issue tracker with the ready-for-agent label.
limitations: It depends on the context already available to the agent.
It does not replace product discovery or stakeholder review.
It needs issue tracker details and label vocabulary from project setup.
It should not publish sensitive conversation details without review.

use_cases.title: Convert planning chat into a PRD
use_cases.description: Create a complete product requirements document after a product manager and engineer define a feature in chat.

use_cases.title: Prepare implementation work for agents
use_cases.description: Document implementation decisions, testing seams, and out-of-scope items before assigning work to an AI coding agent.

use_cases.title: Standardize issue tracker intake
use_cases.description: Turn informal feature discussion into a consistent tracker issue with clear requirements and triage labeling.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic PRD
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after a short feature discussion.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use to-prd to turn this conversation into a PRD. Keep the scope limited to what we already discussed.

prompt_templates.title: Create a PRD from repo context
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after the agent has explored the relevant codebase area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use to-prd with the codebase context from this session. Include implementation decisions and testing decisions from the existing architecture.

prompt_templates.title: Confirm testing seams first
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when test strategy needs explicit alignment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use to-prd and pause after proposing the testing seams. Continue to the final PRD only after I confirm them.

prompt_templates.title: Publish an agent-ready tracker issue
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when project setup and label vocabulary are available.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use to-prd to create the final PRD and publish it to the configured issue tracker with the ready-for-agent label.

output_examples.input: A team discusses adding saved filters to an analytics dashboard.
output_examples.output: A PRD with the customer problem, saved filter workflow, user stories, implementation decisions, testing seams, exclusions, and follow-up notes.

output_examples.input: An engineer and product manager define account invitation changes during a coding session.
output_examples.output: An issue tracker entry that explains invitation roles, email behavior, acceptance states, testing decisions, and items outside the release scope.

best_practices: Review the current conversation for sensitive details before publication.
Confirm the proposed testing seams before creating the final tracker issue.
Keep implementation decisions stable and avoid brittle file path references.
anti_patterns: Using the skill before enough product and engineering context exists.
Publishing the PRD without checking issue tracker project and label setup.
Treating the generated PRD as final approval from stakeholders.

faq.question: Does this skill interview the user for missing details?
faq.answer: No. It synthesizes what is already in the conversation and available codebase context.

faq.question: Can it publish directly to an issue tracker?
faq.answer: Yes, when the project issue tracker and triage label vocabulary are already configured.

faq.question: What sections does the PRD include?
faq.answer: It includes problem, solution, user stories, implementation decisions, testing decisions, out-of-scope items, and further notes.

faq.question: Does it include code snippets?
faq.answer: Usually no. It allows short prototype-derived snippets only when they capture an important implementation decision.

faq.question: Is it suitable for Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should I check before using it?
faq.answer: Check that the conversation has enough context, the issue tracker is configured, and sensitive details are safe to publish.
